messages:
sam: Heads-up — started seeing a spike of Pod restarts in us-west-2 GPU pool after the nightly base-image/toolkit bump. Containers failing with missing libcuda/libnvidia-ml at runtime. Only on node image-2026-03-k6 (kernel 6.1.14).

sam: example crash log from a failed pod:```stderr
Error: cannot open /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so: No such file or directory
[warn] nvidia-container-toolkit: failed to bind mount host libs: mount: permission denied
```

maya: is this the toolkit upgrade we pushed at 02:00? which version?

sam: yep, toolkit 1.12.0 + new base image that includes driver symlink layout changes. deploy-bot rolled to ~40% of nodes.

juan: can you paste the daemonset spec that does the hostPath mounts? wondering about mountPropagation.

sam: here is snippet from nvidia-driver DS:```yaml
hostPath:
  path: /usr/lib/nvidia
  type: Directory
volumeMounts:
- name: nvidia-libs
  mountPath: /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/
  readOnly: true
  # no mountPropagation set (default: None)
```

juan: aha — overlayfs + containerd + the new toolkit now uses host symlinks (..nvidia -> libnvidia.so -> /var/lib/nvidia/...). Without mountPropagation=Bidirectional the bind mount can end up isolated in the container's mount namespace on our overlay root. That would make libcuda invisible to the runtime.

olga: only affects nodes on kernel 6.x? other regions on kernel 5.x seem fine.

sam: correct. us-east-1 nodes are still 5.10 and I don't see the failures there. us-west and ap-southeast 1 (k6) show the problem.

maya: immediate mitigation options? rollback toolkit version or change DS to use mountPropagation? which is lower risk for prod?

juan: short-term: patch the DS to set mountPropagation: Bidirectional on the nvidia-libs mount and rollout to affected pools. That should allow host-level bind mounts / symlink walk to be visible inside containers. Long-term: we need the toolkit vendor to remove relative symlink behavior or adjust packaging.

olga: is mountPropagation safe with our node images / kubelet settings? any clusterwide side-effects?

sre-oncall: we ran mountPropagation in staging last week with no issues, but it does require kubelet >= 1.27? our control plane is 1.26 in some clusters — need to confirm compatibility. Also SELinux/AppArmor could block, double-check.

sam: suggested plan: 1) patch DS to add mountPropagation: Bidirectional, 2) roll to 100% in us-west-2 and ap-southeast-1 only, 3) monitor pod start success and latency for 1h, 4) if still failing, rollback toolkit to 1.11.3 and stop rollout.

deploy-bot: rollout started by maya: nvidia-driver-daemonset patch -> mountPropagation=Bidirectional; targeting nodepool gpu-uw2-2026-k6 (25 nodes)

maya: running node scan to find nodes still with toolkit 1.12.0 and kernel 6.x, will cordon/drain before patching where needed.

juan: also add a readiness probe on the driver DS that lists /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so and /var/lib/nvidia to fail fast if mounts not present. That will reduce noisy pod churn on broken nodes.

olga: can we hotpatch the AMI used by the affected nodepools to 5.x kernel if panic? fallback plan?

sre-oncall: fallback is to stop the rollout and roll nodes back to ami-2026-02 (kernel 5.10) — that's slower but safer if propagation doesn't help.

sam: note for infra: this only surfaced because the new toolkit switched from placing absolute libs under /var/lib to a symlinked host layout. overlayfs handles that differently depending on kernel, so not a pure toolkit bug but a packaging+mount-policy interaction.

maya: monitoring: created dashboard 'gpu.bind-mount-errors' and alert to slack #incidents if >5% failures in 10m.

k8s-ci: quick test matrix suggestion: containerd 1.6 vs 1.7 + overlayfs + mountPropagation flags on kernel 5.10/6.1 to reproduce. I'll run tomorrow.

sam: current status: after mountPropagation patch ~18/25 nodes show healthy and pods start. 7 nodes still failing — investigating if they have older kubelet or custom runtime flags. Will update in 30m.

olga: thanks — if it's not resolved in 60m we rollback toolkit and pause nightlies.

sre-oncall: tagging release-eng and product-security to be aware (drivers can affect compliance stacks).
